questions.content: Name three basic control structures used in algorithms.

A flowchart uses standardized symbols to show the steps of a process.
An algorithm may run forever without producing a result and still be considered correct.
Pseudocode is written in a specific programming language that a computer can run directly.
A rectangle in a flowchart usually represents a process or action.
Sequence means that instructions are carried out one after another in order.
A step-by-step description of an algorithm in plain language that resembles code is called ____.
The flowchart symbol shaped like a diamond is used for a ____.
In the input-process-output model, the results produced by the computer are called the ____.
Which control structure chooses between two or more paths based on a condition?
Which flowchart symbol is typically used to show input or output of data?
Describe in your own words what an algorithm is and name its main properties.
questions.correctAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps that solves a problem. It has clear input and output and is definite (each step is precise), finite (it ends) and effective (each step can be carried out).

questions.content: Name the two main types of computer software.

One byte is made up of eight bits.
ROM is volatile memory that loses its contents when power is turned off.
An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services for application programs.
A monitor is an example of an input device.
The binary number system uses only the digits 0 and 1.
The smallest unit of data in a computer is the ____.
The main circuit board that connects the CPU, memory and other components is called the ____.
A group of eight bits is called a ____.
Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
Which of the following units of data is the largest?
Identify the main hardware components of a computer system and state the function of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Input devices accept data; the CPU processes it; memory (RAM) holds the data and instructions currently in use; storage keeps data permanently; output devices present the results.

Phishing messages often create a sense of urgency to pressure the reader into acting quickly.

Unwanted bulk email sent to many people is called ____.

What does the term netiquette refer to?

Define digital citizenship and state at least three responsibilities of a good digital citizen.
questions.correctAnswer: Digital citizenship is the responsible and respectful use of technology and the internet. Responsibilities include protecting personal information, respecting others online, crediting the work of others, verifying information before sharing it, and reporting harmful behavior.

Define prime numbers and composite numbers, and give two examples of each.
questions.correctAnswer: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself (for example 2, 3, 5, 7). A composite number has more than two factors (for example 4, 6, 8, 9).

questions.correctAnswer: Subtract 3 from both sides to get 2x = 8, divide both sides by 2 to get x = 4, then check by substituting 4 back into the original equation.

questions.content: Name the three common measures of central tendency.
List three types of graphs used to display data.
Name the two main types of data.
Name the four levels of measurement.
List two measures of variability.
The mean is calculated by adding all values and dividing by the number of values.
The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set.
A pie chart is best suited for showing how a whole is divided into parts.
The range is found by adding the largest and smallest values.
A population includes every member of the group being studied.
The difference between the largest and smallest values in a data set is the ____.
A smaller group selected from a population is called a ____.
The ____ is the average of a set of numbers.
Which measure of central tendency is the most frequently occurring value?
Data such as eye color or favorite food are examples of which type of data?
Explain the difference between a population and a sample, and give one example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: A population is the entire group being studied, while a sample is a smaller part of it selected to represent it. Example: all students in a school (population) versus 50 students surveyed (sample).
